name: sleepwatcher
desc: Monitors sleep, wakeup, and idleness of a Mac
why: Hooks macOS sleep, wake and idle events to scripts; a quirky window into system power state, though the project is aging.

brief.what_it_is: SleepWatcher is a command-line tool, a daemon for macOS, that monitors sleep, wakeup and idleness of a Mac. It can run a Unix command when the Mac or its display goes to sleep or wakes up, after a set period without user input, when the user resumes activity after a break, and when a notebook's power supply is attached or detached. It can also put the Mac to sleep and report the time since the last user activity. The homepage lists version 2.2.1, which needs Mac OS X 10.5 or later and includes source code. The homepage describes it as needing a bit of Unix command-line knowledge.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no stated motive. It is one of several small macOS tools the author publishes on a personal page, and it exposes power and idle events so that a user can attach their own scripts to them.
brief.how_it_works: The daemon watches macOS power and idle events and executes a Unix command or script in response. The Homebrew caveats say the sleep and wakeup hooks are read from ~/.sleep and ~/.wakeup when the tool is run via brew services. The homepage does not describe the internals further.
brief.install_notes: The Homebrew caveats say that to make SleepWatcher do anything you must write a sleep script and a wakeup script, located at ~/.sleep and ~/.wakeup when using brew services. The homepage says the 2.2.1 release runs on Apple silicon under Rosetta 2, and that a Makefile is provided to compile a native build. The homepage also names older releases for older systems: 2.0.5 for Mac OS X 10.3 and 10.4, and 1.0.1 for 10.1 and 10.2. The homepage does not list any accounts, runtimes or other setup beyond this.
brief.standout: It exposes idle-time and display-level hooks (display dim, undim, sleep, wake) and lets a plain shell script react to them, which is a rare handle on macOS power state. It is a bare Unix tool with no GUI.
brief.status: Quiet. The homepage says SleepWatcher 2.2.1 is quite old now. The page shows a footer date of 14.07.2026, but no release date for SleepWatcher itself and no commit history were visible to me. I did not check a repository or release page.
brief.caveats: The display options --displaydim, --displayundim, --displaysleep and --displaywakup do not work on Apple silicon Macs, and the homepage says this is still under investigation. On Apple silicon the 2.2.1 build runs through Rosetta 2 unless you compile the native version with the supplied Makefile. The tool needs a user who is comfortable with the Unix command line. The homepage says all software on it is GPL-licensed. The release notes do not say whether the author plans further work.
quotes: is a command line tool (daemon) for macOS that monitors sleep, wakeup and idleness of a Mac.
A little bit knowledge of the Unix command line is required to benefit from this software.
SleepWatcher 2.2.1 is quite old now, but runs fine on Macs with Apple silicon with Rosetta 2 emulation.
